plan.name: Prepare locked repository dependencies
plan.summary: Add dependency preparation for selected parts of the committed repository contract, supporting Go modules, Python requirements pinned by version and SHA-256 hash, and npm lockfiles, including parts with no third-party dependencies; reject floating, inconsistent and unsupported installation forms explicitly. Run each admitted installation in its pinned toolchain with network access only for preparation, stage only declared dependency inputs, and publish reusable environments only after successful installation, unchanged-input verification and immutable image inspection, with cache identity covering all dependency inputs, installation policy, image and platform. Provide an offline consumer for those environments, isolate candidate writes and compilation caches, handle concurrent preparation safely, and charge staging, installation, cache waits and subsequent checks to one bounded allowance with cancellable cleanup. Preserve Invariant's existing module-cache and build-cache behavior, external-plumbing restriction and modeled Python application gate. Update SPEC.md, the README and docs/factory.md to describe this step and its supported formats, boundaries and tests, citing existing supporting decisions in changed SPEC bullets; the merger records the new dependency-preparation decision before the next step because this plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependenciesInstallLockedPartsAndRunOffline
tests.says: Go, Python and TypeScript install their selected locked inputs in the pinned toolchain, return verified immutable environment evidence, and run checks offline with the original argument boundaries and sandbox limits.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependenciesReuseCapturedInputsAcrossCommits
tests.says: Verified environments are reused without installation for identical committed dependency inputs, despite candidate edits or another checkout, and returned evidence cannot change execution authority.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependenciesSelectOnlyNamedParts
tests.says: Only selected parts and their dependency inputs are prepared, repeated names are deduplicated, empty selection does nothing, and unknown or unprepared parts are refused.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyInputReadsObeyCancellation
tests.says: Dependency input reads retain the captured base's bytes and honor cancellation.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyDockerConsumerEnforcesIsolation
tests.says: The default Docker consumer actually launches the immutable environment with no network or image pulls, bounded resources, an overridden entrypoint and no host credentials or unrelated mounts.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyCacheIncludesEveryEffectiveInput
tests.says: Changing lock bytes, another input's bytes or path, install arguments, part directory, pinned image or platform invalidates the cache, and the new environment is reusable.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependenciesRefuseUnlockedAndUnsupportedInputs
tests.says: Missing or inconsistent locks, floating versions, unsupported managers or wrappers, and untracked local, VCS, workspace or recursive dependencies are refused before installation.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependenciesRejectLockRewritesBeforePublishing
tests.says: An installer cannot rewrite a lock and publish a reusable preparation or change the original checkout.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependenciesSupportEmptyDependencyGraphs
tests.says: Go, Python and npm parts with no third-party dependencies produce complete reusable environments and support offline checks.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependenciesHonorExplicitNoInstall
tests.says: An explicit inapplicable installation with no dependency inputs uses a pinned environment without running a network installation.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependenciesAcceptNpmRangesCoveredByLock
tests.says: Ordinary npm manifest ranges are accepted when a consistent complete lock fixes their resolved artifacts.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyFailedInstallNeverBecomesReusable
tests.says: A failed installation is cleaned up and never reused, even when it leaves complete-looking output.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyInspectionRejectsIncompleteAndMismatchedArtifacts
tests.says: Initial publication and reuse require independently verified immutable image, base, platform, recipe and input evidence; missing, corrupt or incomplete evidence cannot satisfy preparation.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyConcurrentCreatorsCannotConsumePartialArtifacts
tests.says: Concurrent creators may wait or install privately, but never consume partial output or share mutable installation resources, and completed output remains reusable.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyCancellationCleansUpWithoutPublishing
tests.says: Cancelling preparation bounds cleanup, removes staged inputs and containers, and prevents reuse of the interrupted install.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyPreparationAndChecksShareOriginalDeadline
tests.says: Multiple cold installations and later checks share the deadline set at preparation entry; expired sessions cannot obtain more time.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyCheckCancellationPreservesVerifiedArtifact
tests.says: Checks inherit the original parent's shorter deadline and cancellation, clean their private resources and preserve previously verified reusable dependencies.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyCandidateStorageCannotPoisonLaterSessions
tests.says: Candidate checks use disposable storage and private compilation caches, so their writes cannot poison a later session's reusable dependency environment.

tests.name: TestRepositoryDependencyBudgetsCannotBeExtended
tests.says: Default and oversized timeout settings never extend preparation beyond the existing sandbox allowance.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and 19 acceptance tests covering isolated, cached dependency preparation for Go, Python, and TypeScript. The checker passed on the first attempt; `repo/` remains unchanged.
